value.rationale: The phase curve sharply quantifies when the natural third-cumulant pole ceases to be globally optimal under variance-preserving signed jump noise. It interpolates between Gaussian smoothing (p=3/4) and the known Skellam endpoint, with explicit quadratic excess and a nontrivial rare-positive-jump law. These are natural concentration quantities and a complete family-level classification, not arbitrary sampled parameters.
